newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds recovered from early losses to close almost unchanged near Friday's levels. Dealers said volume was low with U.S. markets closed for a holiday but saw a recovery in the coming days.
"What we had today was a follow-up of Friday's profit-taking," said a dealer in Madrid. "But now it is more likely the rising trend will resume."

The future contract on 10-year bonds closed little changed and chartists put resistance at 107.40 and support at 107.00 for Tuesday's session. The Bank of Spain was seen maintaining the rate unchanged at its regular money market tender.

But nobody expect that the result, due tomorrow before 0800 GMT, could deliver any surprire. Last Bank of Spain cut was decided on October 3 by 50 basis points to 6.75 percent after an austere 1997 budget package.
On the cash market the 10-year benchmark fell two basis points to 102.95, yielding 7.72 percent, while the spread over the German Bunds was unchanged at 170 basis points.
The short-end part of the curve was gaining with the three year bond rising to 102.86 from 102.83 on Friday, yielding 6.63.
